description: Two-wheeled walking tractor with long steering handlebars towing a flatbed trailer, used for farm hauling and short road trips.

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Two-wheeled walking tractor with an exposed single-cylinder diesel engine over a pair of large lugged wheels, long twin steering handlebars swept back, hitched to a flatbed wooden trailer on two wheels with low stake sides Materials: Bare and rusted steel frame, oil-blackened engine block, mud packed into the lugged tyre treads, sun-greyed and split trailer planks, flaking bright enamel on the engine cowl.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.85. 2,688/4,000 triangles, 4/4 draw calls, 3/3 materials, 4/6 unique geometries, two canvases at 1.7 MB, factory 44 ms. Turntable: enclosed background is the open frame, allowed on measurement.

featureReviews.evidence: Envelope built at 1.54 x 1.36 x 4.18 m against a declared 1.50 x 1.35 x 4.20; stations off the proxy side elevation (engine 0.02-0.22 L, drive wheel 0.10-0.30 L, bars to 0.55 L at 1.00 H, trailer 0.55-0.98 L, trailer wheels 0.78 L).
featureReviews.notes: The proxy is 2.56 lengths tall against the real 3.11; heights are its fractions of H.

featureReviews.evidence: Red tank and gearbox over a black block with a cylinder head, flywheel cover, sump and grille face; a full U bumper loop ahead of the block; two long rusted bars with a cross tube, stays and black grips reaching over the trailer.
featureReviews.notes: Nine solids stepping in and out of each other; the daylight between the bars is flagged by the turntable and allowed on measurement.

featureReviews.evidence: Planked deck, side boards, head and tail boards, six stakes, top rails and chassis beams in grey timber with the plank canvas as map and bump; A-frame drawbar with cross brace and hitch eye converging on the hitch pin; hung on the hitch pivot.
featureReviews.notes: The tow bar reaches the pin from the gearbox; the A-frame belongs to the trailer and yaws with it.

featureReviews.evidence: Two instanced 0.84 m drive wheels, two 0.56 m trailer wheels merged into the trim; pivots wheel-l/r, trailer-wheel-l/r and hitch.

name: Iron Buffalo Walking Tractor
notes: Declared as the tractor plus its trailer together, which is how it is always seen on a road -- the tractor alone is a bare engine on two wheels and reads as a machine part rather than a vehicle. That is why the 4.2 m length. The trailer really does unhitch, but it is left out of destructionGroups because destruction groups are for assemblies the prop breaks into, not for a working hitch; if a consumer needs the trailer separate it should be its own asset.
